name: Zach Lipson
current_role: Investor/advisor, Lightweight Ventures (former co-founder & Chief Product Officer, Dutchie)
profile: Serial entrepreneur who co-founded Dutchie in 2017 with his younger brother Ross; as chief product officer he helped build it into the leading cannabis e-commerce/point-of-sale platform (valued ~$3.75B in 2021). The brothers left Dutchie in early 2023; he has since invested in and advised early-stage startups.
interesting_fact: Dutchie started in Bend, Oregon; within two years it served 450 dispensaries in 18 states and was pitched as 'a Shopify of the cannabis space maybe meets DoorDash'. Ross described Zach as the methodical one: 'Zach is the one who wants to make sure that we're doing everything right.'
notes: No longer at Dutchie (left Feb 2023; the founders later filed suit against company leadership, so avoid framing outreach around Dutchie's current management). Low public profile; LinkedIn is the likely route. Appeared on the 'To Be Blunt' cannabis podcast (ep. 020).

name: Sammy Krikler
current_role: Co-founder, Chief Insurance Officer and board member, Earnix
profile: Israeli statistician and co-founder (2001) of Earnix, whose AI-driven pricing and rating software is used by insurers and banks to price policies and loans. He is the only one of the three co-founders still at the company, which became a unicorn in 2021 after a $75M round led by Insight Partners.
interesting_fact: Earnix's CEO Udi Ziv has called Krikler 'the brains of the product'; of the three 2001 co-founders (with Yoni Cheifetz and Shai Fogel) he is the one who stayed for two decades-plus.
notes: Very low media profile. Aggregator profiles say he studied statistics at the Hebrew University and was R&D manager at Eventus Software before Earnix (unverified primary source). Route via Earnix press/marketing or LinkedIn.

name: Laurent Ritter
profile: French entrepreneur who co-founded Paris mobile-game publisher Voodoo with Alexandre Yazdi in 2013. Voodoo became a hyper-casual gaming giant (Goldman Sachs and Tencent invested) and was valued around $2B. Ritter is also an active angel investor in European startups.
interesting_fact: Voodoo, which he co-founded in 2013, grew from a small Paris studio into one of the world's most-downloaded mobile game publishers, popularising 'hyper-casual' games.
notes: Low public profile; Yazdi is Voodoo's public face (CEO). Investor databases describe Ritter as an ESC Rennes alumnus who runs an angel vehicle called Purple (not verified from a primary source). Current operational role at Voodoo unclear.

name: Felipe Delgado
current_role: Co-founder (CFO/President), Merama; partner and board member, Beetmann Energy
profile: Mexican finance executive who co-founded Merama in 2020, a Mexico City/São Paulo group that acquires and scales leading Latin American e-commerce brands; its 2022 Series B valued it at $1.2B. Before that he was CEO/CFO of Beetmann, a Mexican wholesale-electricity supplier and renewable-energy developer using AI/IoT to optimise energy use.
interesting_fact: He has an energy background unusual for an e-commerce founder: he ran Beetmann Energy, a qualified supplier in Mexico's wholesale electricity market that develops renewable plants, and remains a partner and board member there.
deep_cut_fact: He began his career in J.P. Morgan's US Oil & Gas investment-banking group, holds a UT Austin BBA (Walter B. Smith Scholar) and a Harvard MBA, and is a keen runner who has completed two marathons; Quién named him a 'Titan of Business' among its 50 people transforming Mexico (2022).
notes: Strong energy-podcast angle via Beetmann. Titles vary by source (CFO vs President). Low media profile; LinkedIn or Merama is the route.

name: Jordan Feldman
profile: Harvard-educated former Goldman Sachs banker who co-founded Rightway (c.2017), a New York healthcare-navigation and pharmacy-benefits company combining clinician-led support with an app to help members find high-quality, cost-efficient care. Rightway reached a unicorn valuation and Feldman remains CEO.
interesting_fact: He co-founded Rightway with his father, physician Dr. Theodore Feldman (its chief medical officer); his father's experience as a doctor inspired the clinician-led model.
deep_cut_fact: Before healthcare he worked on Goldman Sachs' Mortgage Trading and Investment Banking teams, then left to help found RedBird Capital Partners, Gerry Cardinale's private-equity firm; he holds an A.B. in Government and Economics from Harvard.
notes: Speaks at Conference Board events; reachable via Rightway's press/marketing team or LinkedIn.

name: Dave Merkel
current_role: Co-founder and board member, Expel (stepped down as CEO Nov 2026; succeeded by Steve Kelley)
profile: Cybersecurity veteran who co-founded Herndon, VA managed detection-and-response firm Expel in 2016 with Yanek Korff and Justin Bajko and led it as CEO for a decade to a $1B+ valuation. Previously CTO of Mandiant and then FireEye after their 2014 merger. In November 2026 he handed the CEO role to Steve Kelley and stayed on the board.
interesting_fact: Expel's founders said they started it because they couldn't buy the security service they wanted: 'a few practitioners left to build the service they wished they could buy.'
deep_cut_fact: He started his career as a special agent in the US Air Force Office of Special Investigations doing cybercrime and digital-forensics investigations, then built the first incident-response capability for AOL and Time Warner.
notes: Just transitioned out of the CEO seat (GovInfoSecurity, 10 Nov 2026) -> may have more time for a podcast. Frequent RSA Conference speaker; blogs on expel.com.
